(KCTV) - Kansas Governor Laura Kelly and Lieutenant Governor David Toland announced a new international partnership, signing a Statement of Mutual Cooperation with the Czech Republic. Gov. Kelly says the agreement opens the door to expanded collaboration between Kansas and the Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Industry and Trade across four key industries: Aerospace Agriculture, animal health and biotechnology Advanced manufacturing Nanotechnologies State leaders note that the deal is meant to strengthen trade, business development and technological research between the two partners - and to create new economic opportunities for entrepreneurs, business, scientists, artists and universities on both sides. Why It Matters Kansas already has deep Czech roots. Officials say the state is home to several Czech-owned businesses and the town of Wilson - known as the Czech Capital of Kansas and one of the largest Czech-American communities in the U.S. ALSO READ: Missouri voters, Secretary of State clash over ballot petitions Leaders add that the agreement gives that longstanding relationship a formal framework to grow. What They’re Saying Governor Kelly credits the Kansas Department of Commerce for building the international ties that made the agreement possible. “I am proud of the work the Kansas Department of Commerce has done to strengthen Kansas’ ties with our partners across the globe,” Kelly says. “This Statement of Mutual Cooperation will benefit the people of both the Czech Republic and Kansas for years to come.” Lt. Governor Toland, who also serves as Secretary of Commerce, adds that the deal gives existing Kansas-Czech business relationships room to expand. “This Statement of Mutual Cooperation marks an exciting new chapter in the relationship between Kansas and the Czech Republic,” he notes. “Kansas already has strong ties with Czech industry, and this agreement gives us a real framework to build on that momentum and create economic opportunities for both Kansans and Czechs for years to come.” Kansas flag (KWCH) The Czech Republic’s top diplomat on the trip points to the growing presence of Czech companies already doing business in Kansas. “Relations between the Czech Republic and Kansas have deepened significantly in recent years,” states Czech Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Jiří Brodský. “The statement of cooperation expresses our shared determination to elevate this partnership to a higher level, and I am very pleased that successful Czech companies are already operating in Kansas.” State lawmakers are also voicing support, with one representative framing the agreement around economic competitiveness. “The strongest economies are built on strong relationships. This statement expresses the mutual interest to create new opportunities for Kansans to innovate, collaborate, and compete while deepening our longstanding friendship with the Czech Republic,” Representative Rui Xu, District 25, says. Another legislator brings a personal connection to the signing, citing both her committee role and her own Czech heritage. READ MORE: Feds charge Interim Jackson County Executive Phil LeVota with offering six-figure job to bribe opponent out of 2026 race “As a member of the House Commerce Committee and someone with Czech roots, I’m proud to support this Statement of Mutual Cooperation between Kansas and the Czech Republic,” Representative Laura Williams, District 30, says. “This agreement will help strengthen long-term relationships and create new opportunities for trade, innovation, investment, and job growth across Kansas.” What’s Next Officials have not announced a specific implementation timeline. Check back for updates as the Kansas Department of Commerce moves forward with next steps under the agreement. Copyright 2026 KCTV. All rights reserved. The drone was detected shortly after midnight Monday, triggering air-danger alerts in and around the capital, Vilnius, as well as nearby districts. Lithuania’s public broadcaster, LRT , reported that authorities activated NATO fighter jets after the object was spotted near the Trakai area, west of Vilnius. About 30 minutes later, the drone was destroyed in the air over a rural area near the village of Pratkūnai in Kaišiadorys district, between Vilnius and Kaunas, according to LRT. Preliminary information indicated that the drone entered Lithuania from Belarus and was traveling west. “A drone that just entered Lithuanian airspace was destroyed by NATO fighter jets,” President Nausėda said in a statement . “I thank Allied personnel for their swift response.” Article continues below the player Military police, police officers and other authorities were sent to search for debris and determine what type of drone it was, its capabilities and its intended target.
